details.description: Nova is Deepgram's general-purpose speech-to-text model and the predecessor to Nova-2. Deepgram describes it as trained "over 100 domains and 47 billion tokens." Deepgram's Models & Languages Overview lists Nova under "Legacy Models," alongside Enhanced and Base, with Nova-2 as its successor.
advantages: Deepgram describes Nova's training as spanning "over 100 domains and 47 billion tokens."
disadvantages: Deepgram lists Nova under "Legacy Models" in its Models & Languages Overview, with Nova-2 as its successor.
Deepgram reports that Nova-2 achieves an 18.4% reduction in word error rate (WER) versus Nova-1.
use_cases: General-purpose transcription of everyday audio across a broad range of domains.

sources.title: Nova-2: Automatic Speech Recognition, Reinvented | Deepgram

notes: Treated 'nova' as Deepgram's Nova-General model (as opposed to the nova-phonecall/nova-medical variants, which are separate catalog entries). No standalone maker-published WER figure for Nova itself was found; only Nova-2's own page states its improvement relative to Nova-1, which is cited here as a disadvantage of Nova. Legacy status confirmed via developers.deepgram.com/docs/models-languages-overview's section headings. The catalog carries no deprecation_date. Verify pass: the Nova-2 launch post calls Nova-2 itself (not Nova) 'the deepest-trained automatic speech recognition (ASR) model in the market' ('...Nova-2 continues to be the deepest-trained...'); the prior advantages sentence misattributed that superlative to Nova at its own release, so it was corrected to keep only the supported training-scale figure.
